stem:
Aarav looks at the diagram: a flat arrangement of six rectangles labelled $A$–$F$.

Which claim correctly decides whether this arrangement is a valid net for a cuboid?

options.text: It is a valid net: the six faces fold into a cuboid with no overlaps, and joining flaps are not counted as extra faces.
Call it a net even when the faces cannot meet edge-to-edge when folded from paper or cardboard.
Accept it as a net only because it has six regions, even if some faces would overlap when folded.
Call it a net only because the word net is the most obvious printed label near the diagram.

teacher.key_rationale: A valid net folds into the solid without face overlaps; flaps are not extra mathematical faces. Skipping foldability, counting regions alone, or grabbing the printed word miss the hinge.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source cuboid net as a labelled six-rectangle cross net for a cuboid.
